newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania police block new bid to grab Hungary flag.
newsitem.headline: Romania police block new bid to grab Hungary flag.

text.p: Police on Wednesday thwarted the second attempt in as many weeks, this time backed by a large crane, to seize a national flag from the newly-opened Hungarian consulate in the central city of Cluj.

Witnesses said police ordered the crane's driver to move out of the square where the consulate was opened a week ago by the two countries' foreign ministers despite fierce opposition from Cluj's Romanian nationalist mayor.
After a stand-off lasting several minutes, the driver complied and several dozen people in the square dispersed without incident.

The reopening of the consulate, shut by communist dictator Nicolae Ceausescu in 1988, is seen as further consolidation of relations between the two traditional central European rivals after the signing of a historical treaty last year.

Romania is home to 1.6 million ethnic Hungarians who live mostly in Transylvania and view Cluj as the cradle of their culture. Many Romanians had long believed Hungary wanted to restore control over Transylvania, which it ruled until 1918 under the Austro-Hungarian empire.
Last week, the red, white and green Hungarian flag was snatched from the consulate by three men later found to be Cluj city employees.
Mayor Gheorghe Funar, twice an unsuccessful candidate for Romanian president, denied any involvement in that incident.

But Funar told reporters before Wednesday's confrontation that he wanted the consulate closed and would take measures to remove the flag for good. He cited a post-Communist law banning the display of foreign flags on private buildings.
Elected to a new term as mayor last year, Funar has antagonised ethnic Hungarians, who make up a quarter of the Cluj's 300,000 residents, by curbing their linguistic and cultural rights.
